A lead of this magnitude is indeed significant in the context of the game, especially with the surface likely to deteriorate over the coming days. Whether or not the pitch breaks down as expected remains to be seen, but New Zealand have put themselves in an advantageous position, forcing India to respond under pressure. With still 3 more days left in the Test, the tourists would ideally want to bat the hosts out of the game here and close all doors of a potential Indian comeback. Back in a bit for New Zealand's second innings.

A superlative bowling effort from New Zealand! Mitchell Santner proudly holds the ball aloft as he leads his team off the field, having delivered a stellar performance. His seven-wicket haul has helped his side bowl India out for just 156 to gain a crucial lead of 103 runs. The visitors didn't take long to wrap up the Indian innings after the Lunch break. Ravindra Jadeja briefly threatened to mount a counter-attack, but Santner swiftly nipped that in the bud before going on to clean up the tail. The damage had already been done in the first session, where Santner was relentless, leaving the Indian batters reeling under his spell. He was well-supported by Glenn Phillips who chipped in with a couple of wickets.

Right then, a commanding first session has put New Zealand firmly in control of the proceedings. Mitchell Santner set the tone early, challenging the Indian batters with tight lines and variations in pace. Quickly adapting to the conditions, he found the ideal speed to bowl on this surface and consistently hit probing areas, ultimately reaping the rewards. Glenn Phillips joined the fray shortly after the drinks break and wasted no time in adding to India’s woes. Indian batters, attempting to counter the mounting pressure by going on the offensive, often succumbed, gifting wickets to the disciplined Kiwi spinners. Santner, in particular, was instrumental, creating relentless pressure that made each boundary attempt a risk India couldn’t afford.

PITCH REPORT - Simon Doull and Dinesh Karthik are pitchside. Doull begins by saying that the weather is pleasant and a bit cooler today. Karthik points out an interesting stat - all 10 New Zealand wickets fell from the pavilion end in the first innings. He observes that the surface hasn’t changed much but expects more turn as the game progresses. Karthik emphasizes the importance of speed for the spinners, mentioning that India’s spinners were successful bowling in the 84-94 kph range. He advises against bowling too quickly, as it might reduce the amount of turn or purchase from the pitch. For New Zealand, he suggests that Santner, Ajaz, and Phillips stick to this effective speed range. From India’s perspective, Karthik feels the batters will need to watch out for the natural variations that the pitch can produce.

Day 2 promises to be a classic tussle between bat and ball. Expect India’s batters, particularly Gill and Jaiswal, to counterattack once they see off the first hour or so. New Zealand’s bowlers, especially Southee, will be looking to exploit reverse swing if there is any on offer later in the day, and as mentioned earlier, the spin twins Patel and Santner will be pivotal in shaping the day’s outcome. So sit tight as this intriguing Test match continues to unfold. Today could provide the defining and all the more riveting moments throughout the day!

For New Zealand, Rachin Ravindra’s 65 and Devon Conway's 76 were the standout performances in their innings, but they collapsed from a strong position where they lost the last 7 wickets for 62 runs. On Day 2, New Zealand will rely heavily on their spinners, especially Ajaz Patel and Mitchell Santner, who have already found assistance from the pitch. The surface is offering turn and bounce, and they’ll look to pressurise India’s middle order early. If they can strike early blows in the first session, New Zealand could surge ahead in the game.

India’s performance on Day 1 was highlighted by Washington Sundar’s remarkable 7-wicket haul, dismantling New Zealand’s batting lineup and limiting them to 259. His return to Test cricket after three and a half years was nothing short of spectacular. However, India’s response with the bat started shakily, losing Rohit Sharma early. As they resume at 16/1, Shubman Gill and Yashasvi Jaiswal will be key players to watch, tasked with stabilising India’s innings. The top order needs to navigate through spin-friendly conditions, and a strong partnership could tilt the momentum India’s way.

Washington Sundar is up for a chat. He says that he manifested this for a long time of getting a chance to get back into the side and it happened in this Test. He further adds that he always wanted to stay accurate with whichever batter he bowled and that helped him to pick up 7 wickets. He talks about the pitch saying that it was dry and was expected to spin from day 1. Ends by saying that the wickets of Rachin Ravindra and Daryl Mitchell gave him a lot of confidence.

Sundar registered his career-best figures of 7/59 in 23.1 overs, leading India’s resurgence after a challenging first half of the day. From what seemed like a comfortable position at 197/3, New Zealand suffered a dramatic collapse, losing their last 7 wickets for just 62 runs and ultimately being bowled out for 259. In response, India lost their skipper early to an absolute peach from Tim Southee. It didn't take long for Tom Latham to introduce spin, which posed immediate questions for both batters. Shubman Gill and Yashasvi Jaiswal faced a nervous period against the two Kiwi spinners, but they managed to hold their ground and see out the day.

India’s bowlers appeared to be struggling, as Conway and Ravindra were content to milk the singles and occasionally find the boundary. However, just when the Indian fielders began to look flat, Ashwin provided a much-needed breakthrough, nicking off Conway. Despite that wicket, India’s defensive approach allowed another partnership to build, but Washington Sundar turned things around with two crucial strikes towards the end of the second session, halting New Zealand's charge. India carried that momentum into the third session, with Sundar picking up where he left off. Although the ball wasn’t turning sharply, Sundar extracted enough movement off the pitch to chip away at the Kiwi middle and lower order.

Earlier in the day, after winning the toss, Tom Latham had no hesitation in opting to bat first. The Kiwi openers got off to a solid start, navigating the new ball without much difficulty. India managed two breakthroughs in the first session through Ravichandran Ashwin, but consistent pressure eluded them due to the in-out fields, allowing the visitors to rotate the strike and keep the scoreboard ticking. In the second session, New Zealand continued to score at a steady pace, with Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra both cruising to their fifties.

End of an enthralling day of Test cricket! It began encouragingly for New Zealand with the bat, but India fought back brilliantly, led by a stellar bowling performance from Washington Sundar. As a result, they will be the slightly happier side at the end of Day 1. Despite winning a crucial toss, the visitors will be disappointed to have posted only 259, especially given their promising position at one stage. Their bowlers though kept things tight and consistently probed the batters during the 11 overs.
